name: Bitcast

paragraphs: A miner on Bitcast’s YouTube mechanism publishes public videos that meet a brand’s brief and keeps a server reachable on a public IP address, using port 8091 by default. The miner works with a registered hotkey, the key a miner works with, and connects a YouTube Partner Program channel through OAuth credentials or Bitcast’s keyed token service. The channel must be at least 21 days old, have 100 to 500,000 subscribers, and reach 1,000 minutes watched and 10% average percentage viewed over 90 days. The cited passages give no hardware minimums or additional miner fees.

About every four hours, validators, the participants who score the miners’ work, check how well videos fit the brief and use seven-day averages to score growth in YouTube Premium revenue. The 14-day scoring window and three-day analytics delay give a 17-day age cutoff. Dollar scores determine reward shares after caps and smoothing, and unused rewards go to burn UID 0. The README assigns roughly 2% to YouTube and 98% to X, while the code reads the chain split and uses 85% if that lookup yields unusable data.

Creators can publish from three days before a brief starts through its final day, but restricted briefs pay only listed channels, and videos flagged as having captions fail screening. The cited passages give no registration protection period. Read from https://github.com/bitcast-network/bitcast at commit b8af435 on 2026-11-23.
mining_note.how_it_was_made: This note was put together by AI agents and not by a person who mines here. One agent read the subnet's public repository and wrote down what a miner does, what it takes and how the work is paid, with a source for each statement, and a second agent opened every source and took out whatever it did not support. Of 32 source checks, 28 held, 4 did not hold and 0 could not be opened, and only what held is in the text above. Nothing of the subnet's code was run, and the note describes the code as it stood on the day and at the commit named in its last sentence, so it can be out of date.
